english: A wooden door blocks your path.
Like, HEAVILY locked. This mechanism is pretty solid.
Whoever put this up really did not want anyone getting inside...
That means you should avoid it. It's probably trapped.
HE SHUT it- all to keep his PEOPLE at bay.
An OWNER in fear of his LABOR...
You're getting all that from looking at a locked door?
Your scarf wiggles slightly. "Not trapped! Meek knows!"
That must lead to the back-office. Haven't been in here before, but I think they closed down a while ago.
Heard rumors from some goblins that worked here- I think the owner fired them all out of nowhere.
You approach the locked door once more.
What did you expect? For it to magically open itself?
...Yeah, that's actually concerning now that I think about it.
I'll ask around later. Nothing to worry about now, though.
Your fingers work the mechanism with precision.
You fumble with the lock, your tools slipping.
Your hands are too clumsy for this delicate work.
Try again. Or find another way.
You slam your shoulder against the wood.
The door frame splinters and gives way!
You throw yourself against the door.
You speak the words of power.
A deep booming sound echoes through the rollermill.
The lock clicks open with a satisfying pop.
You see nothing but black beyond.
Can't see a damn thing in there.
The scarf's eye slops around your head.
No. Not dungeon. No traps here!
You stumble inside, carefully allowing your vision to get used to the complete darkness of this underground...
Why don't I take the lead.
Your light cuts through the gloom.
Broken crates. Scattered papers. A mess of abandoned equipment.
You notice the ceiling. Several glow-stones lie shattered on the floor.
The explosion. It must have shaken them loose.
That tea shop blast reached even here.
Your fingers brush against walls. Around obstacles.
Eventually your eyes adjust to the faint light from the doorway.
You can make out shapes now.
Broken crates. Scattered papers. A complete mess.
And on the floor... shattered glow-stones.
They must have fallen from the ceiling when the tea shop exploded.
You stumble forward into the darkness.
Suddenly, the left-most side of your left-most foot connects with something hard.
You can see shapes now. Vaguely.
The storage chamber is a disaster.
Broken equipment. Scattered papers. Shattered glow-stones on the floor.
The tea shop explosion must have knocked them from the ceiling.
This place has been abandoned for some time.
Meek smells old human-scent. Very old!
You sift through papers and crates.
Most of it is worthless. Old receipts. Inventory lists.
They tried to form an Azgal union.
That explains why this place is empty.
The owner shut down rather than deal with organized labor.
Fire everyone and close up shop.
But the world rarely gives people what they deserve.
That's how you run a business.
Or at least, as old as factory work. It's bourgeoisie bullshit, all the way to the top.
He shakes his head. "Ignore me, I'm getting tired here."
You continue deeper into the chamber.
At the back, you find an office.
Old papers. Ledgers. More termination notices.
The drawer slides open with a snap.
Inside lies a smooth stone. One with several faces adorned on its sides.
It pulses faintly with esoteric energy.
You slip the Pebble into your pouch.
This place has given you all it can.
I'm not finding anything else here.
Meek will help find exit! Come, come!
You make your way back through the darkness.
